title: Never take over a live user host lock, and release only a run's own
summary: A lock held by a live run for more than 10 minutes is no longer taken over: when `ia host claude --user` finds its lock, `<IA home>/claude/.lock`, held by another run whose pid is still running, @inventarch/distribution now refuses IA-DIST-INSTALL-BUSY however old the lock is, since its age does not show that its owner stopped. A lock whose pid has died is still taken over at any age, and one whose pid is empty or unparseable after 10 seconds; a lock holding 0, a negative number or a number above 2147483647 is now judged the same way, where 0, a number above 2147483647 or below -2147483648 and, on POSIX, -1 or the negative of a live process group used to wait out the 10 minutes, and any other negative number was taken over at once. A stale lock whose pid another process has since reused now stays busy until it is removed by hand, as the unchanged IA-DIST-INSTALL-BUSY message says to do when no run is active. A run now writes its pid, a space and a random token, and at its end removes the lock only while it is still a regular file holding exactly that text and its name still names that file, so a run whose lock was replaced no longer removes the replacement and lets another run acquire the lock while the replacement's owner is active. A lock in the earlier format, a pid alone, is still judged by its pid, and a run's release leaves it in place. Earlier releases running at the same time still take over a lock older than 10 minutes and, when they finish, remove whatever lock is at the path, so two runs can still overlap until every CLI using that IA home is upgraded. Brief windows between a takeover's or a release's check and its removal remain, as Node has no unlink-if-same: two runs that take over the same stale lock at the same moment can both end up holding it. Liveness is judged in each run's own pid namespace, so a run in a container or on another host sharing the IA home can still take over a live run's lock.
